chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Mukhtār narrated from him, عليه السلام, that he said:

I am a mu'adhdhin, so when it is a cloudy day and I do not know the time, he said: “When the rooster crows three consecutive calls, then the sun has passed its zenith and the time of salat (prayer) has entered.”

key_terms.زَالَتِ ٱلشَّمْسُ: the sun has passed the zenith, marking noon
key_terms.مُؤَذِّنٌ: the caller who announces the prayer
key_terms.وَقْتُ ٱلصَّلَاةِ: the beginning of the prescribed prayer time
key_terms.يَوْمُ غَيْمٍ: a cloudy day when the sun is obscured
key_terms.ٱلدِّيكُ: the rooster used here as a natural sign

ai.seo_question: How can the time of noon prayer be known on a cloudy day in hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a practical sign for identifying the beginning of the prayer time at noon when the sky is cloudy and the sun's position cannot be directly determined. It reflects a jurisprudential concern for preserving correct prayer times through observable natural indicators.
